hook: Over six decades, 17-year-old Elizabeth Tyler's lost photographs of Coventry bomb sites stayed hidden in an attic box.

sections.voiceover: Over six decades, 17-year-old Elizabeth Tyler's lost photographs of Coventry bomb sites stayed hidden in an attic box.
sections.visual_cue: Close up of an old dusty wooden attic box opening in dim light.
sections.sfx_cue: Creaking wooden lid opening with a dusty thud

sections.voiceover: In 1963, 17-year-old Elizabeth Tyler wandered through Coventry photographing bomb sites. Working with waitress wages, she bought a second-hand 1933 Rolleicord camera. How'd Elizabeth Tyler's photographs survive?
sections.visual_cue: Archival photograph of 1960s Coventry bomb ruins.
sections.animation_cue: Slow zoom into the archival photograph

sections.voiceover: Those rare images survived being moved through four countries.
sections.visual_cue: Map graphic showing multiple international borders crossed.
b_roll: Historical map of Europe migration routes
sections.animation_cue: Dotted line tracing movement across borders

sections.voiceover: She developed her films at the Coventry College of Art darkroom. That archive spent 6 decades untouched in an attic box.
sections.visual_cue: Series of vintage black and white prints laid out on a wooden table.
sections.animation_cue: Pan across the spread of photographs

sections.voiceover: Explore Elizabeth Tyler's 1963 Coventry bomb site archive.
